reviewType: Read-only cross-review of renderer and persistence changes; author review of MPR framing implementation; actual GPU screenshot comparison
verifiedBehavior: MPR signal fitting is a display-only source-signal extent, not anatomical segmentation or source cropping. Complete source image fit remains directly selectable and resets zoom to 100%.
All three MPRs retain equal millimetres per pixel. Pointer, public-goal and surgical overlays use the same physical view bounds as source GLSL sampling.
Mirrored and oblique source affine tests preserve RAS/native agreement; blank RAS bounding-box corners outside the actual source grid are not selectable.

MRI gradient extinction uses central-difference source gradients transformed as physical covectors, and is enabled only for automatic MRI transfer with explicit shell style. CT and authored custom transfers bypass it.
Floating-point LUT retains low extinction values; hosts without float-linear filtering use nearest filtering rather than unsupported GL filtering.
Source shell material shares its enabling uniform with depth-peel clones. Fully opaque layers retain solid rendering. The depth-peel NoBlending path does not force fragment alpha to one.

Native scan switching restores saved per-scan slice framing. Shell style is shared with study anatomy appearance. Python and TypeScript settings validators admit both new settings and reject malformed values.
Corrected complete acquisition tooltip wording to complete source image so published preprocessed CTA is not presented as original uncropped acquisition.

Final CT skull/context handling uses exact declared packed context membership rather than treating all contrast-enhanced voxels above a scalar threshold as bone; hidden declared contexts cannot be resurrected by the legacy intensity-only fallback.

mprVisualReview.legacyFrameScope: The archived mri-initial failure frame was reviewed for MPR framing only; its legacy 3D state is not evidence for the new context style.
observations: Default 100% fit produces visibly larger heads than v1, filling approximately 78–84% of available image height in the reviewed MRI view. Previous duplicate header padding is eliminated.
Skull/head envelopes remain within the default panes. Explicit 125% zoom brings portions of the envelope to pane edges and clearly displays 125% badges, supporting the choice of default 100%.
Full image and scan-content fit are visibly distinguished in the toolbar and each slice header. Scale bars and neurological orientation labels remain legible.

limitations: The Medivis reference patient, source coverage and lesion differ; shape similarity is not an anatomical accuracy test.
All-source inferred T1CE vessel estimates remain dense and include conspicuous peripheral/inferior fragments. Rendering polish does not improve source labeling accuracy or establish complete vessels.

Content fit excludes low signal and very sparse tails for framing. It must not be interpreted as preservation of all signal within the initial viewport; complete source remains available through full image fit.
Existing viewport rounding can cause subpixel differences between fractional CSS overlays and integer GL viewport pixels. No new discrepancy was introduced by the fit helper.
CTA high-attenuation context is a threshold estimate, not a verified bone class. It can cover non-bone high-attenuation source voxels.

The high-complexity context retains the original source surface, so terracing/coarseness is visible. Smoother visual similarity must not be obtained by inventing missing branches or changing source masks.

The final ivory CTA opening is brighter and more uniform than the neutral grainy Medivis reference; the MRI vessel estimate remains dense and noisy. No visual parity or anatomical accuracy is claimed.
status: Pass with documented visual and source limitations; no new blocking correctness issue identified
reviewerIndependence: Reviewer authored MPR framing and tests, and independently cross-reviewed the separate renderer, persistence, native-source integration and captured GPU evidence.
observedImprovements: MRI source heads occupy materially more of each tile than v1, with default 100% content fit preserving a visible envelope. Explicit zoom, full-image recovery and state badges work in captured GPU interaction runs.
MRI shell mode reduces the previous gray interior and face haze while keeping a source-supported head outline and visible cyan tumor.
The final segmentation-only muted magenta brain rim distinguishes the estimated brain boundary from the outer neutral head envelope and brings the visual hierarchy closer to the Medivis reference.
Native CTA now displays sourced arterial labels in rust and venous labels in blue against restrained acquired CT context, with much better branch visibility than the initial ivory veil.

Final opaque high-attenuation context is ivory rather than the earlier orange transfer. An axial cutaway exposes the published source-supported interior with visible rust/blue labels and a light outer rim.

visualAssessment.acceptance: Visibly closer to the supplied Medivis segmentation and CTA compositions, without visual or anatomical parity.
visualAssessment.mri: Final left view has less haze and a separate magenta source-brain boundary; linked MPR heads are substantially larger than the v1 images.
visualAssessment.cta: Rust/blue vessel labels and the ivory axial opening are legible in the final native GPU screenshots. The result remains more terraced and has substantially fewer labeled branches than the reference.
visualAssessment.defaultZoom: 100% is appropriate. The 125% screenshots visibly reach pane edges; the default should not silently zoom farther.
visualAssessment.controls: Framing selection, reset/zoom, orientation and physical scale remain visible in the reviewed desktop captures.

sourceFaithfulness.statement: Published preprocessed braincase-cropped and LPS-reoriented CTA, with source arrays/affine retained in the native pipeline. It is a separate case, not fabricated MRI angiography or an uncropped original DICOM acquisition.
sourceFaithfulness.annotation: Arterial and venous labels are published partial, unreviewed source annotations. Missing left ICA/MCA source classes and unannotated branches have no inferred cause and are not synthesized.
sourceFaithfulness.highAttenuationContext: The layer internally named bone is explicitly displayed as high-attenuation CT context, a threshold estimate rather than a reviewed anatomical skull segmentation.
sourceFaithfulness.surfaceFallback: The context surface has 1,112,624 vertices and 2,184,544 triangles; source-restored fallback retained its original positions with maximum display displacement 0 mm. Vessel display displacements remain bounded near 0.238 mm.
sourceFaithfulness.fixity: All reviewed full GPU reports preserve source hashes; the current native CTA manifest also independently matches the source-QC manifest hash.

mprGpuEvidence.interpretation: Agreement is with displayed physical scale and cursor readout, supported separately by analytic mirrored/oblique CPU-vs-GLSL mapping tests. This does not establish diagnostic image registration accuracy.
mprGpuEvidence.persistence: Full-image 125% framing, shell style, source selection, cursor, layers, source scope and camera survive native save/reopen in the reviewed report.
